region.name: Pillar ACH Ops Reviews
region.summary: Q3 status meetings, MBRs, QBRs, and Pillar ops syncs tracking the ACH pipeline cut-over and Sidekiq decommission, the KYC migration, the investing beta rollout, the Sep 26 duplicate round-up incident, and the ops sync handover from Marcus to Sarah Kim.

brief.text:
Pillar ACH Ops Reviews covers the recurring governance cadence around the Pillar Bank ACH relationship during Q3 and early Q4 2026. That cadence includes the mid-quarter check-in, Eng Staff meetings, the September Pillar MBR, the Q3 QBR on Oct 2, and the weekly Pillar ops sync. The arc starts at the Aug 17 mid-quarter check-in. There, the ACH cut-over had slipped to Aug 18 after a failed load test, the KYC migration was on track, and investing was moved to early September pending Pillar sign-off, with a decision to launch it first as a 5% MTU beta. By Eng Staff on Sep 8, several things had moved. The investing beta was live to 5% of MTU under Pillar's $2,500 daily cap. The new ACH pipeline had run three weeks with zero missed cutoffs, and a Sidekiq decommission plan was being drafted. The KYC migration was closed. Eng Staff also noted a SOC 2 readiness review set for Sep 10 with expected findings, a growth experiments freeze that Kavi dissented on, and the engagement of Hollis Partners for the VP Eng search.

The September Pillar MBR, which included Karim Haddad, closed the ACH pipeline's 30-day hold with approval to delete the old Sidekiq ACH code. It reported investing beta metrics of 5,050 invited, 38% funded, and about 3% hitting the $2,500 cap. Pillar received a proactive heads-up on a reconciliation discrepancy: 0.4% of positions were off by fractional shares after a DriveWealth corporate action. Pillar compliance may view this as a control weakness. The MBR also covered Series B status, BIN pricing, QBR planning, and the decision that Sarah Kim would take over the ops sync from Marcus Bell. Maya wanted Sarah to run two syncs with Marcus shadowing first. On Sep 26, duplicate round-up debits hit customers, and Pillar was notified within 24 hours. The round-up sweep has been protected by a duplicate/idempotency check since then. At the Oct 2 QBR, the team reported zero missed cutoffs in 45 days since cut-over. Other outcomes were that investing GA was retargeted to Oct 20, the card soft launch slipped to Q1 2027, and Pillar requested a written remediation plan for the Sep 26 incident.

The Oct 2 ops sync was Sarah Kim's first as owner. ACH metrics were healthy: all files went out before cutoff, the return rate was 0.31%, and investing transfers made up about 6% of items, under the cap. NACHA-cutoff alert noise is to be tuned. Sidekiq ACH deletion is planned for Oct 16, with notice due Oct 13. The written remediation plan, owned by Maya, is due to Pillar by Oct 15. ADR-032 next steps all belong to Sarah: send the settlement-timing question to Renee and Kavi, raise round-up file volume with Theresa at the Pillar ops sync, and circulate the design for decision. Open risks are SOC 2 gaps (owner Sam Whitfield, highest severity), Marcus being overloaded, a pattern of money-movement incidents, and the reconciliation discrepancy likely blocking investing GA (owner Devon). Typical questions this region answers include when the Sidekiq ACH code is being deleted, what ACH and investing metrics Pillar saw, what Pillar asked for after the Sep 26 incident, who now runs the Pillar ops sync, and what could block the Oct 20 investing GA.
